personas.name: Andrej Karpathy
personas.reason: Keeping up 4 habits: Steering mid-turn, Spec with criteria, One-shot spec and 1 more.

personas.name: Steve Yegge
personas.reason: Tried something new: Agent team, Swarm, Beads as the plan.

moments.title: Steering mid-turn
moments.what: You sent a correction or more context while the agent was still working, without stopping it.
moments.try: You don't have to wait for the agent to finish. Type while it works: the message reaches it mid-turn, so a wrong assumption is fixed before it turns into twenty edits.

examples.note: sent while the agent was working
sent while the agent was working
sent while the agent was working

moments.title: Interrupt and redirect
moments.what: You stopped the agent and gave it a new direction within two minutes.
moments.try: When the agent heads the wrong way, press Esc and say what you want instead. Stopping early is cheaper than undoing later.

moments.title: Takes the other branch
moments.what: You rewound the conversation, or forked the session, to try a different route.
moments.try: When a turn went wrong, rewind to before it (Esc Esc) instead of arguing with the result: the failed attempt leaves the context.

moments.title: Grounded prompt
moments.what: Your prompt named files the agent then worked on.
moments.try: Name the files, functions or commands that matter. The agent spends fewer tokens searching and guesses wrong less often.

moments.title: Shows the evidence
moments.what: You pasted an error, a stack trace or a screenshot instead of describing it.
moments.try: Paste the actual error output or a screenshot. It is the most precise context you can give, and it costs nothing to write.

moments.title: Spec with criteria
moments.what: You wrote a structured prompt with constraints or acceptance criteria.
moments.try: For anything bigger than a quick fix, list what done means: the constraints, what must not change, how to verify it. The agent then checks its own work.

moments.title: One-shot spec
moments.what: A detailed prompt that the agent carried out in one go, with no correction afterwards.
moments.try: Front-load the thinking: one well-specified prompt usually beats five rounds of corrections, in quality and in tokens.

moments.title: Vibe one-shot
moments.what: A prompt of a few words that led to real edits, with no correction afterwards.
moments.try: Once the agent knows the project, a short prompt can carry a lot. Try a one-liner for a change you both understand well.

moments.title: Clean slate
moments.what: You cleared the context to start the next task fresh.
moments.try: Starting something new? /clear first. Old context is paid for on every call and distracts the agent.

moments.title: Plans first
moments.what: You had the agent plan before it touched any code.
moments.try: Use plan mode (Shift+Tab) for anything non-trivial: you review the approach before a single file changes.

moments.title: Compacts on purpose
moments.what: You compacted the context yourself, at a moment you chose.
moments.try: Context grows with every call, and so does the price of each call. Run /compact at a natural break, saying what to keep, before auto-compaction picks a worse moment.

moments.title: Right model for the job
moments.what: You switched the model or the effort in the middle of a session.
moments.try: Not every task needs the largest model. Switch with /model: a smaller one for mechanical work, the largest for hard reasoning.

moments.title: Own commands and skills
moments.what: You ran a skill or a slash command that you or a plugin added.
moments.try: Typing the same instructions again and again? Make them a skill or a slash command and run them with one word.

examples.note: ran a command of your own
ran a command of your own
ran a command of your own

moments.title: Builds the harness
moments.what: You had the agent edit its own instructions, skills, commands or settings.
moments.try: When you correct the agent twice for the same thing, put the rule in CLAUDE.md or a skill. The fix then holds in every session after.

moments.title: Context isolation
moments.what: A subagent did the reading in a context of its own and came back with a summary.
moments.try: Send exploration to a subagent: it reads twenty files in its own context and returns a page, so the main context stays small and cheap.

examples.note: a subagent made 14 calls in its own context
a subagent made 14 calls in its own context
a subagent made 14 calls in its own context

moments.title: Model routing
moments.what: A subagent ran on a cheaper model than the session's main one.
moments.try: Subagents that search or summarise rarely need the largest model. Give them a smaller one and pay a fraction.

moments.title: Parallel sessions
moments.what: Several of your sessions were working at the same time.
moments.try: While one agent works, start another on an independent task in a second terminal. Two to five at once is where many experienced users settle.

moments.title: Worktrees
moments.what: An agent worked in a git worktree of its own.
moments.try: Parallel agents in one checkout trip over each other's changes. Give each one its own git worktree.

moments.title: Background agents
moments.what: Agents worked in the background while the session carried on.
moments.try: Long work (a test suite, a broad search) can run as a background agent while you keep talking to the main one.

examples.note: an agent ran in the background
an agent ran in the background
an agent ran in the background

moments.title: Automation
moments.what: Agents ran headless or on a schedule, without you typing.
moments.try: Some work doesn't need you in the loop: run the agent from a script or CI (claude -p), or schedule a recurring check.

moments.title: Ships
moments.what: A session opened or linked a pull request.
moments.try: Let the agent take a change all the way: branch, commit, push and open the pull request.

moments.title: Plugged in
moments.what: The agent used tools from an MCP server.
moments.try: Connect the agent to the systems you work in (issue tracker, docs, browser) over MCP, so it can look things up itself.

moments.title: Agent team
moments.what: You ran teammates: agents that stay around and take more work.
moments.try: An agent team splits a big job over teammates that message each other. Start with two or three on clearly separate parts.

moments.title: Workflow
moments.what: A scripted workflow fanned the work out over many agents.
moments.try: When the same multi-step job comes back, script it as a workflow and let it run the agents.

moments.title: Agents spawning agents
moments.what: Agents started agents of their own.
moments.try: For tree-shaped work, let a coordinating agent hand pieces out to subagents of its own.

moments.title: Swarm
moments.what: Five or more agents ran at the same moment.
moments.try: Independent pieces of work (one per package, one per test file) can run as many agents at once. Watch the bill.

moments.title: Beads as the plan
moments.what: The plan lived in beads: issues created, linked and closed.
moments.try: A plan in markdown gets rewritten over and over. Beads (bd) keeps it as a graph of issues that agents claim and close across sessions.

moments.title: Persistent personas
moments.what: You woke a persistent persona: a named agent with its own memory, whose day ends with sleep rather than an exit.
moments.try: Sessions are days, personas persist. Give a recurring role a persona that wakes with its memory and open threads, works a bounded day and sleeps, instead of starting from nothing each time (Yegge's model-welfare essay).

moments.title: Forks itself
moments.what: The agent forked copies of itself that started with its whole context.
moments.try: A fork starts with everything the agent knows. Use one for a side quest that needs the full picture.

moments.title: Two harnesses
moments.what: You worked with both Claude Code and Codex in the same week.
moments.try: Each harness has its strengths. Trying another one on a real task shows you what your main one does well.

moments.title: Night shift
moments.what: Agents kept working for hours while you were away.
moments.try: Hand over a well-specified, well-tested task before you leave, and come back to the result.
